integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the run's own application directory. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, public search, or unexplained network activity was detected.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Workflow: 65 file changes, 1 build/test/browser verification actions.

overall.summary: A complete single-file rigid-body crash lab. Every mandatory default is exact, the solver is deterministic, and the instrument panel reads like real telemetry. Accessibility of the settings panel is the only real gap.

standards.summary: 1,868 lines organised into clearly separated solver, scene and UI sections with no randomness anywhere in the physics path, so repeated runs are bit-identical.

findings.title: Solver iteration counts are tuned by heuristic, not measured
findings.detail: Velocity and position iteration counts are derived from the row count with hand-picked constants and clamps. This holds across the documented range but has no guard if a future range change pushes the wall taller. Document the stability envelope next to the clamp.

strengths: No Math.random anywhere: the baseline experiment is fully deterministic
Sequential-impulse solver with separate velocity and position passes
Depth layers modelled as independent collision groups rather than a single flat wall
Impact kinetic energy derived from mass and speed instead of hardcoded

specification.summary: All thirteen mandatory defaults are present at the exact required values, the five required settings are exposed with the required min/max ranges, and telemetry covers speed, elapsed time and moving bricks.
strengths: Car speed 22, cols 12, rows 8, layers 2, brick mass 2.5, brick 0.50x0.24, g 9.81, friction 0.72, restitution 0.18, car 1250kg/4.2x1.45, ground friction 0.85, scale 80 px/m all exact
Settings ranges match the brief exactly (speed 5-45, cols 4-24, rows 3-16, layers 1-5, mass 0.5-12)
Default wall and car are already on screen before the first Test press
Staggered brick courses with half-bricks at the row ends

ux.summary: The control bar, telemetry readout, metre scale and keyboard hints make the experiment legible, but the settings panel is built from bare inputs with almost no ARIA.

findings.title: Settings sliders carry no programmatic labels
findings.detail: The parameter panel is generated from a config table into raw range inputs. Only two ARIA attributes exist in the whole document, so a screen reader announces unlabelled sliders. Bind each label to its input or add aria-label from the config row.

findings.title: No reduced-motion path
findings.detail: Camera shake and dust particles run unconditionally. Honour prefers-reduced-motion by damping the shake while keeping the simulation itself intact.

strengths: Telemetry pre-computes impact energy so the outcome is predictable before the run
Keyboard shortcuts documented on screen (SPACE run, R reset, S settings)
Slow-mo control makes the collision inspectable
Metre scale bar and pixels-per-metre readout make the scene measurable
